pageScopeQualifications.1685: Title Electrical Actuators, printed Lecture 53, footer 1.
pageScopeQualifications.1686: Learning outcome only: understand electrical actuators.
pageScopeQualifications.1688: Right-hand rule figure and F vector = I vector cross B vector viewed. The text explicitly defines F as force per unit length, not total force. A conductor need not translate macroscopically to experience force; moving charge/current suffices. General straight-conductor force includes length and sine of field angle.
pageScopeQualifications.1689: DC/AC classification, force F=BIL and a length-L conductor figure. Scalar law assumes perpendicular conductor and uniform field. Moving-conductor induced EMF requires the appropriate nonzero flux-cutting component. Broad modern-DC prevalence is context dependent and differs from the later industrial AC-servo summary.
pageScopeQualifications.1690: Faraday equation e=−dφ/dt and Lenz explanation. Printed phrase oppose the charge producing it is a typo; following text refers correctly to change in flux. One-turn flux versus total flux linkage must be declared. Not every induced EMF is a motor back EMF.
pageScopeQualifications.1691: Two rotating-loop diagrams, N left/S right, active-side opposing forces form a couple. Current reversal at the vertical passage sustains torque sense. Zero resultant force can coexist with nonzero torque.
pageScopeQualifications.1692: Slotted armature, field poles, segmented commutator, carbon brushes and four-pole diagram viewed. Coil-current switching sustains rotation. Reversing armature current or field current alone reverses electromagnetic torque; reversing both does not.
pageScopeQualifications.1693: PM constant-flux model, F=BIL, effective N conductors F=NBIL, T=Fb=NBILb=Kt I and Vb=Kvω. Figure labels L and active-side separation b. N is the source effective conductor factor, not an invitation to count both sides twice. Kv here is a back-EMF constant, not rpm/V speed constant.
pageScopeQualifications.1694: Series equivalent circuit R,L,Vb, neglected-inductance current (V−Kvω)/R, torque Kt(V−Kvω)/R. Torque-speed lines for V2>V1 and current-torque linear plot inspected. Zero-load zero-torque is the ideal no-loss model; physical no-load friction needs torque/current. Initial zero-speed proportional torque is quasi-steady, not instantaneous current jump with nonzero inductance.
pageScopeQualifications.1695: Series-wound circuit and qualitative curves. Reversing supply reverses armature and field together. Under unsaturated flux proportional to current, torque is proportional to current squared; the displayed convex-up current-versus-torque plot does not quantitatively match that model. Unloaded overspeed is a risk, not a recommended experiment.
pageScopeQualifications.1696: Shunt parallel-field prose, starting/regulation/reversal points and curves. Drawing places Ra/La before the field branch, unlike the usual independent shunt field and armature branch; preserve as a source topology issue rather than teach it as a wiring schematic. Constant-flux torque proportional to armature current is not the displayed curved current-torque plot. Near-constant speed is approximate, not exact load independence.
pageScopeQualifications.1697: Compound series/shunt prose, circuit, three torque-speed curves and full comparison table. Prose says highest starting torque while table labels compound average, a direct local conflict. Table shunt high field resistance/good controllability/average start; series low/poor/high; compound high parallel and low series/average/average. Qualitative comparison, not a universal motor rating.
pageScopeQualifications.1698: PM motor cutaway labels encoder, commutator, magnet, ironless winding, brush, reduction gearhead and output shaft. PM field does not imply brushless. No field excitation power is needed, but winding/friction and drive losses remain. Relative efficiency and torque/weight claims are design dependent.
pageScopeQualifications.1699: Speed-control prose and PWM pulse figure inspected. PM current determines torque within the linear model; speed also depends on voltage/back EMF/load. PWM varies average applied voltage at fixed supply. A duty ratio is not generally the same percentage of loaded speed.
pageScopeQualifications.1700: H bridge S1 upper-left, S2 upper-right, S3 lower-left, S4 lower-right. Diagonals S1/S4 and S2/S3 reverse motor voltage; same-leg simultaneous conduction shorts the rail. Source BJT A/B drive example and freewheel diodes inspected. Base terminology is BJT-specific; dead time and current paths need engineering design, not this simplified sketch.
pageScopeQualifications.1701: Two full feedback diagrams viewed: forward digital controller→DAC→analogue amplifier→motor in both; tachogenerator analogue feedback→ADC→controller above; encoder digital→code converter→controller below. Encoder replaces the analogue feedback conversion, not the pictured forward DAC. Feedback alone does not guarantee stability.
pageScopeQualifications.1702: BLDC diagram shows permanent-magnet rotor N/S and stator coil sectors A,B,C,D. Electronic sequential coil switching replaces brush/commutator wear and sparking. Three sensors are the illustrated sensored implementation, not a universal requirement. The last line mentions base current, specific to the transistor example.
pageScopeQualifications.1703: Full tree inspected: single-phase low-power and polyphase high-power branches each divide into induction and synchronous. Relative cost/control-difficulty assertions are broad historical/general statements, not specification rules. Frequency sets synchronous field speed; induction rotor speed also depends on slip.
pageScopeQualifications.1704: Induction motor as transformer: stationary primary/stator, rotating secondary/rotor, air gap. The text broadly says AC motor rotor power is induced; the heading and mechanism apply to induction motors, not every synchronous AC motor. Brushed DC conduction statement does not define all brushless DC variants.
pageScopeQualifications.1705: Cage diagram and text: copper/aluminium bars and end rings close rotor circuits; no external rotor electrical connection; stator windings driven by AC. Ideal single main-winding rotor at rest has zero net starting torque, hence auxiliary starting methods. This is not a claim that every packaged single-phase motor lacks a start arrangement.
pageScopeQualifications.1706: PM synchronous rotor and stator winding diagram. One pole-pair example rotates one mechanical turn per electrical cycle. More pole pairs reduce mechanical speed at fixed frequency. PM rotor is an example, not every synchronous machine. Bare fixed-frequency starting difficulty does not exclude inverter-controlled startup.
pageScopeQualifications.1707: Stepper PM rotor and two perpendicular winding axes W1/W2 diagram inspected. Pulse count sets nominal position and pulse rate speed, conditional on no missed steps. Full list 12,24,72,144,180,200 steps per turn corresponds to 30,15,5,2.5,2,1.8 degrees. PM versus variable-reluctance is the presented classification, not exhaustive of hybrid designs.
pageScopeQualifications.1708: VR rotor is ferromagnetic, aligns to low reluctance/high flux. Diagram shows eight stator poles A,A-prime through D,D-prime and six rotor teeth, with A/A-prime excited. Phase means independent stator winding, not individual tooth count. Step angle is per specified switching transition. Powered holding torque differs from unpowered detent torque; the source reversing-spindle clause is not a separate definition requirement.
pageScopeQualifications.1709: Six selection factors: speed range, torque-speed variation, reversibility, duty cycle, starting torque, power. Servo graph has distinct driver-peak, motor-continuous and commutation-limit curves. At 2000 rpm and about 1 N m a point is above the continuous boundary but below the peak curve; do not infer continuous suitability from a peak rating. Plot is illustrative, not a motor datasheet or exact numeric specification.
pageScopeQualifications.1710: Operating point is motor/load torque-curve intersection. Declining motor curve and rising load curve depicted. Self-regulation follows their local slope relation under a positive-inertia mechanical model; not every arbitrary intersection is stable.
pageScopeQualifications.1711: Below pictured equilibrium motor torque exceeds load and accelerates; above it load exceeds motor and decelerates. Changing supplied voltage shifts the motor characteristic and equilibrium. Generic source claim needs an admissible stable operating point and operating limits.
pageScopeQualifications.1712: Full dense summary read including new coreless category, DC wheel/conveyor/pan-tilt examples, AC induction and PMSM/VFD examples, servo encoder plus closed-loop position control, possible sub-0.01-degree accuracy, AC industrial-servo prevalence, stepper open-loop basic operation, microstepping and printers/plotters/SCARA/lab uses. Accuracy is possible not guaranteed, and microstep command resolution is not actual accuracy. Categories overlap: coreless is construction, servo is a controlled system.
